faq.a: No sound can travel through the near-empty space between planets and stars, because there are almost no particles to carry it. Inside a spacecraft full of air, sound works normally.
asks: Do explosions make noise in space?

faq.q: Why can't sound travel in a vacuum?
faq.a: Sound is vibrations passed from particle to particle. A vacuum has no particles, so there is nothing to pass the vibrations along.

faq.q: How do astronauts talk to each other in space?
faq.a: They use radios in their suits. Radio waves are a kind of electromagnetic wave, like light, and travel through empty space without needing air.
asks: How do astronauts communicate on a spacewalk?

faq.q: How did scientists prove sound needs air?
faq.a: In 1660 Robert Boyle placed a ticking watch inside a glass jar and pumped the air out. The ticking got fainter and fainter, showing that sound needs air to travel.
asks: What is the bell jar experiment?

faq.q: Why do space films have explosion sounds?
faq.a: Film makers add sounds because silent space battles feel strange to audiences. In real space, explosions would be silent to anyone watching from a distance.
asks: Would a spaceship make noise in space?

facts: Robert Boyle showed in 1660 that a ticking watch in a jar becomes silent as the air is pumped out.
Radio waves are electromagnetic waves and can travel through a vacuum; sound waves cannot.

quiz.say: Two astronauts on a spacewalk have broken radios. How can they hear each other speak?
quiz.show: With broken radios, two astronauts could hear each other by…
quiz.why: Sound can travel through solid helmets that touch, even though it cannot cross empty space.

wrong.0: However loud they shout, there is no air outside to carry the sound.
wrong.2: Facing each other does not help; space between them carries no sound.
